# Aleppo Codex Line Breaks

Where the manuscript line breaks fall in the Aleppo Codex pages that contain the Book of
Job, and in a run of Deuteronomy pages. (In manuscript studies this is sometimes called
"line-by-line alignment" of a text to a manuscript image.)

This note describes the retained data: what it covers, what its files hold, and how it
was made. The marking is finished. The programs and page scans it used were retired on
2026-09-26 by
[`../../doc/PLAN-retire-codex-index-image-work.md`](../../doc/PLAN-retire-codex-index-image-work.md),
so nothing regenerates this data. Until then this file was the marking procedure;
`git show f4d81285:aleppo/doc/aleppo-line-breaks.md` recovers that version, and
`git show f4d81285:<path>` recovers each retired program.

## Folder layout

```
MAM-basics/
  aleppo/
    line-breaks/            ← flat-stream JSON files with line markers, one per page
    column-coordinates/     ← per-page column quadrilaterals
    ds-flat-stream/         ← flat streams with no line markers
    check_line_breaks.html  ← the frozen report of the last line-break check
  MAM-simple/               ← the landed MAM-simple product
```

## Data format

Line-break data lives in `aleppo/line-breaks/<page>.json`. Each file
is a flat JSON array (a "flat stream") containing:

- **Structural markers:** `{"page-start": "270v"}`, `{"page-end": "270v"}`
- **Verse markers:** `{"verse-start": "Job 1:16"}`, `{"verse-end": "Job 1:16"}`, and
  `verse-fragment-start` and `verse-fragment-end` where a page begins or ends mid-verse
- **Parashah markers:** `{"parashah": "spi-pe2"}`
- **Words:** plain Hebrew strings, MAM's atoms, split after every maqaf
- **Line markers:** `{"line-start": {"col": "1of2", "line-num": 1}}`,
  `{"line-end": {"col": "1of2", "line-num": 1}}`
- **Blank lines:** `{"blank-line": {"col": "1of3", "line-num": 16}}`, for a line with no
  verse content

A column is named in NofM form: on a two-column page `1of2` is the right column and `2of2`
the left, a three-column page has `1of3` to `3of3`, and a one-column page `1of1`. Each
column's lines count from 1 to 28.

A file without line markers, such as those in `aleppo/ds-flat-stream/`, is the starting
point the flat-stream generator wrote; one with them has had line breaks defined by hand.
The generator read `MAM-simple/xml-vtrad-mam/` with the segmentation that
`get_verse_atoms` in `py/mb_cmn/mam_xml_verses.py` now gives, and
[`reading-mam-simple.md`](reading-mam-simple.md) describes the reader's choices.

## Page image sources

The retired scans came from the full Aleppo Codex scan at
`https://archive.org/details/aleppo-codex` (CC0 license, 593 pages), through the direct
image API:

```
https://ia601801.us.archive.org/BookReader/BookReaderImages.php?zip=/7/items/aleppo-codex/Aleppo%20Codex_jp2.zip&file=Aleppo%20Codex_jp2/Aleppo%20Codex_{NNNN}.jp2&id=aleppo-codex&scale={S}&rotate=0
```

- `{NNNN}` = zero-padded page number (see leaf table below)
- `{S}` = scale factor: `1` = hi-res (~2.5 MB), `2` = medium (~800 KB)

For Job leaves (all past extra leaf 241a), the formula is:

```
N = (leaf_number - 1) × 2 + 2 + (0 for recto, 1 for verso)
```

[`../aleppo-pages-provenance.md`](../aleppo-pages-provenance.md) records the download and
the last commit that holds the scans.

mgketer.org is useful for quick lookups but chapter-based, not page-based:

```
https://www.mgketer.org/mikra/29/{chnu}/1/mg/106
```

(Job = book 29, `chnu` = chapter number.)

## How the line breaks were marked

Each page's flat stream was generated from MAM-simple, and the line markers were then
added by hand in an interactive editor that showed the stream beside the page image,
cropped to one column. Line numbers were assigned per column. Both the editor and its
merge step were deleted on 2026-09-26, before the rest of the retirement;
`git show 4ac4f16a:py/py_ac_loc/gen_line_break_editor.py` recovers the editor.

## Line break heuristics

- Job's poetic sections are laid out in two columns (stichos-based).
- Early verses often fit **one verse per line**.
- Longer verses often span **two lines**, breaking at an etnachta or
  other major accent.
- Lines can break at a maqaf (the maqaf stays on the line).
- Parashah breaks (`{פ}`, `{ס}`) may cause blank lines.

## Pages with line breaks defined

All 24 Job pages (270r–281v) have line breaks defined for both columns
(28 lines per column). `aleppo/line-breaks/` also retains the separately contiguous
Deuteronomy run 001r–006r. The strict MAM-simple comparison checked those two
runs separately: no JSON file represents the text between Deuteronomy 34 and
Psalms 149.

The check's MAM-simple sequence comparison omitted U+05BD and U+05BF and no other
code points. U+05BD serves as either meteg or silluq; U+05BF is rafe.
`no_marks_comparison_key` was narrowed to those code points on 2026-09-08, in
`c76239a5`. Every other mark, every format character, and all punctuation,
including maqaf, PASEQ, and sof pasuq, had to match. The pointed JSON strings
remain the page's display and transcription data, and the comparison did not
normalize Hebrew. The frozen report, `aleppo/check_line_breaks.html`, lists 91
issues; `139f631e`'s message records them as structural line-marker issues, with
the word-sequence check against MAM-simple passing.
